$comment: Circuits (tours) covered by the app. Add a tour by appending an entry — nothing in the model/API logic hardcodes these ids.

history.$comment: How much history to ingest by default and where the raw CSVs live. `startYear` is the earliest season pulled by `npm run update-data` (override with --from). Serve/break stats exist in Sackmann data from ~1991 onward. `mirrors` lists alternative GitHub repos to git-clone if the primary one is unreachable from your network.
history.rawBaseUrlsComment: Tried in order. jsDelivr is a CDN that mirrors GitHub file-by-file and is usually reachable on networks that filter raw.githubusercontent.com — it still serves the ORIGINAL repo, so the data is current.
history.mirrorsComment: Alternative GitHub repos to try if the primary one is unreachable. Deliberately EMPTY: JeffSackmann/tennis_atp and tennis_wta are 404 (deleted, not blocked — another repo on the same account still serves), and the mirror that used to be listed here, stakah/tennis_atp, is 404 as well. A mirror entry that does not resolve is worse than none: it turns one clear failure into two, and the retry advice it produces sends you to a page that no longer exists. Add one back only after checking it actually serves a recent season.

sackmann.$comment: JeffSackmann/tennis_atp stopped being publicly reachable (404), so ATP history now comes from Tennismylife/TML-Database: same column layout, one CSV per season, updated through the current year, and it carries each player's official rank/points on every match row.

There is no WTA source left on GitHub. JeffSackmann/tennis_wta is 404 and TML covers ATP only, so this block will fail and update-data falls through to tennis-data.co.uk, which serves both tours (plus closing odds) and reaches the current season. The repo is kept here rather than deleted so that the attempt — and its 404 — is visible in the log instead of the WTA silently having no source at all; and so it starts working again by itself if the repo ever returns.
